findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Not applicable to this change; open finding must remain tracked until physical root cause is identified and closed.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Users may continue to encounter tags that are reported verified but later appear blank or do not persist. The new diagnostics may not by themselves resolve the open contradiction, and no automatic rewrite is provided.
findings.EVIDENCE: Package evidence: 'physical': 'UNKNOWN mismatch -> read-only re-tap Verified -> process restart blank. Original UID not retained; root cause unknown. HIGH finding spoolio-m1-persistence-contradiction open.' Change text: 'No write algorithm changes.' Source shows only recordRead metadata additions; no change to write persistence or verification logic.
findings.FINDING: The previously identified high-severity physical persistence contradiction remains open; this remediation adds only metadata diagnostics and does not identify or fix the root cause of non-persistence or blank tag after restart.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Continue root-cause investigation of M1 physical persistence; ensure diagnostics capture sufficient mutable state and persisted context to close the high-severity finding in a future remediation.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: 1. Record a read. 2. Force-stop/restart the app. 3. Verify the latest report appears in NfcPanel before any new NFC interaction. 4. Verify history contains no more than 20 reports and includes UID, capacity, writable, tech, discovery-cache and active-RF summaries.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: After process restart, the global UI shows no report until a new tag is read, so the added metadata cannot be used to diagnose the state just before restart or the blank verified tag.
findings.EVIDENCE: NfcCoordinator.kt declares `var readDiagnostic by mutableStateOf<String?>(null); private set` and only sets it inside `recordRead` during tag handling; no code reads the `history` value from SharedPreferences 'nfc-read-diagnostics'. The history is written with `commit()` but never restored. Physical evidence includes 'process restart blank'.
findings.FINDING: Persisted NFC read diagnostic history is never loaded or displayed after process restart, defeating the purpose of diagnosing the process-restart blank outcome.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: On NfcCoordinator initialization, load the latest persisted report (and expose the most recent 20 entries) into `readDiagnostic` or a dedicated diagnostics history UI. Ensure it appears without requiring a new tag tap.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Force `commit()` to block for 500ms in a test build; attempt a write with a tag that remains in field. Verify the write still completes without TagLost or state change and that the diagnostic report is recorded after the write decision.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: The additional I/O and hashing can delay the state machine reaching WRITING and the `writeNdefMessage` call. If the user removes the tag during this delay, Android may throw TagLost/IOException and produce an unnecessary WRITE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN or write interruption, despite the write algorithm itself being unchanged.
findings.EVIDENCE: In NfcCoordinator.handle, `recordRead(tag, ndef, current, "inspection")` is executed immediately after reading NDEF and before `machine.inspected(...)` and the subsequent `ndef.writeNdefMessage(...)`. `recordRead` calls `messageSummary` which performs SHA-256 serialization/hashing and `diagnostics.edit().commit()` on the single-threaded IO executor. For an armed write or overwrite consent, this synchronous work occurs while the tag must remain in the RF field.
findings.FINDING: Synchronous SharedPreferences commit and NDEF digest in `recordRead` are inserted before write state transitions; added latency in the active write path may increase tag-loss or write failure.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Move diagnostic recording off the critical write path: defer SharedPreferences persistence until after the NFC interaction completes or use asynchronous `apply()`/batching; avoid blocking the IO thread before a write operation.
